extracted.intended_audience: public relations students and practitioners (especially those working with educational institutions, associations, and labor unions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for public relations practice in education settings, associations, and labor unions, describing target publics, communication tools, program objectives, and activities practitioners should undertake. Emphasizes crisis topics, stakeholder management, use of digital analytics, and integration with fundraising and advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication topics in education
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation-related issues can escalate into crisis communication situations. Depending upon the type of school, a crisis might include the broader separation of church and state issue, determining when freedom of expression becomes hate speech, violence on campus, disputes between teacher unions and school administration, decisions of elected governing boards, and clarifying the role of the school in social issues such as sex education and providing condoms on campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and prepare for these specific sensitive topics when planning communications for educational institutions; tailor crisis plans to the kinds of controversies likely in the institution's context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effective communication on limited budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: While public relations clearly plays a more central and vital role in the education sector, the continuing issue of unstable funding streams affects the function’s ability to meet and manage expectations on shoestring budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find creative and resourceful ways to engage and inform stakeholder groups when budgets are constrained (see guidance on digital tools below). Be realistic about resource limits when setting goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and prioritize diverse stakeholder groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Professionals must find creative and resourceful ways to engage and inform a broad array of stakeholder groups that range from parents with the child’s best interest in mind to elected officials that want the best schools possible in their district. Yet another important stakeholder group are labor unions, which represent teachers/faculty, administrative staff, and service employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map stakeholder groups (parents, school staff, students, business leaders, community members, alumni, boards, elected officials) and tailor messages and channels to each group's needs and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of websites, email, and social media for targeted messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Money for printed publications and materials has all but disappeared in many K-12 and community college school districts, so public relations professionals now take advantage of technology to inform and engage stakeholders and target publics. Websites and email marketing have long been de rigueur, with social media having taken the entire public relations field by storm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, YouTube, and similar platforms to quickly push out highly targeted messages or respond to issues, focusing on smaller, influential key publics when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build and maintain relationships with reporters and bloggers
rubrics_metrics.description: The changing media landscape and the evolving nature of social media impact the way public relations professionals interact with reporters who cover education. The emergence of bloggers, who are often not professional journalists, but have powerful voices nonetheless, and the decreasing number of reporters covering education require the professional to be more diligent than ever in building solid professional relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate strong professional relationships with the remaining beat reporters and influential bloggers; be proactive and reliable as a source to gain media trust and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be thoughtful and timely in social media responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media and its impact on journalism have produced greater accountability on the part of educational institutions, '…teaching us new lessons in being relevant and timely, but also more thoughtful and careful before responding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond quickly where needed, but exercise care and thoughtfulness to avoid hasty or harmful communications. Consider approval and review processes for sensitive social posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure reach and engagement with analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology-based tools such as the World Wide Web, email, and social media provide inexpensive means of measuring reach and evaluating engagement. Programs such as Google Analytics or Webalizer allow one to examine measures such as the number of unique visitors, what pages were visited, and for how long. Social media utilities indicate the number of fans or friends and permit active engagement among followers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track web metrics (unique visitors, pageviews, time on page) and social metrics (fans, followers, engagement) to evaluate content effectiveness and refine messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use face-to-face communication when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite their cost-effectiveness and versatility, social media, the Internet, and email cannot replace old-fashioned face-to-face communication. Teachers may not have time to sort through dozens of emails; parents want to meet teachers; traditional school open houses still command attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate in-person events (open houses, town halls, face-to-face meetings, video conferences) into communication plans—especially for audiences less reachable or persuadable online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty, accessibility, and transparency as constants
rubrics_metrics.description: Honesty, accessibility, and transparency remain constants in effective public relations, and sometimes the best way to convey these are through face-to-face engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make these values explicit in messaging and behavior across channels; prioritize transparent communication during issues and crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior leadership must support and be public face
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an elementary school principal or college president, the leaders of academic institutions must recognize that public relations is a required part of the job and that they are often the public face of an institution. Almost a third of university and college presidents say that they meet more frequently with their public relations officers than with any other member of the management team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage senior leaders in PR strategy and equip them to act as visible spokespeople; their involvement is key to establishing relationships and public support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify key target publics (education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key target publics for education include: Parents; School staff, from principal or president to teachers to custodian to administrative staff; Students; Business leaders and owners; Community members at large; Alumni; Elected or appointed boards of trustees; Local, state, and federal elected officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list to ensure communications planning covers all primary internal and external audiences; tailor tactics and messages to each group's roles and concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand higher education sector issues affecting PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues unique to higher education include rising operating costs and expectations, competition for private support, admissions vs. diversity tensions, faculty recruitment challenges, and declining/unpredictable public funding affecting tuition and access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate awareness of these structural issues into messaging, fundraising, reputation management, and stakeholder communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate public relations with alumni and development functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations staff at colleges and universities must work in tandem with colleagues in alumni association and fund-raising functions to collaborate in developing messages and strategies to achieve 'friend-raising' and fund-raising goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate branding, messaging, and outreach with development; align PR campaigns to support fundraising and alumni engagement objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation management and brand-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners spend a great deal of time on reputation management and enhancing the university’s brand image, which includes building trust among internal and external stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize long-term trust-building activities, consistent branding, and proactive reputation monitoring and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage perceived credibility of associations
rubrics_metrics.description: To the media and other publics, associations often have more credibility than individual companies or public relations firms because, correctly or not, they are perceived as less self-serving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use association status strategically in media outreach and advocacy to increase message persuasiveness; maintain ethical behavior to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: provide members with helpful information
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide members with helpful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design member-focused content and channels that address practitioners’ informational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: recruit new members
rubrics_metrics.description: To expand the association by recruiting new members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outreach campaigns, benefits communication, and events to attract and convert potential members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: harmonize member viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: To harmonize member viewpoints by promoting positive positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop consensus-building communications and emphasize shared values to present unified positions externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: promote industry or profession
rubrics_metrics.description: To promote the industry or profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create campaigns that highlight the profession’s contributions and bolster public esteem and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: influence legislation and regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: To influence government legislation and regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in public affairs and advocacy communication, provide credible information to policymakers, and coordinate member mobilization where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: improve products and services
rubrics_metrics.description: To improve products and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate industry standards, member feedback channels, and collaboration initiatives to raise quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: gain popular support and combat adverse publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: To gain popular support and combat adverse publicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proactive media relations, issue framing, and public education to mitigate negative coverage and build public backing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: train recruits and provide continuing education
rubrics_metrics.description: To train recruits and provide continuing education for all members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop educational programming, certification, and professional development communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: sponsor public service programs
rubrics_metrics.description: To contribute to social progress by sponsoring public service programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and promote CSR-style initiatives that advance social causes relevant to the association’s mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association PR goal: promote member behavior standards to enhance credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To promote behavior standards among members that will enhance credibility and stave off government regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and enforce codes of ethics and standards; communicate compliance and self-regulation efforts transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: prepare and disseminate technical and educational materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing and disseminating technical and educational publications, videos, and other public information materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an editorial calendar and quality standards for member- and public-facing publications and multimedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: sponsor conventions, seminars, and exhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsoring conventions and meetings, instructional seminars, and exhibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use events for networking, member development, revenue generation, and message amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: handle government contacts and interpret actions to members
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling government contacts and interpreting to members the legislative and administrative actions of government agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely briefings, regulatory summaries, and advocacy toolkits for members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: compile and publish relevant statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Compiling and publishing relevant statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate industry data and reports that support advocacy, research, and media pitching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: prepare and distribute news, information, and PSAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing and distributing news, information, and public service announcements to the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop press materials and PSA campaigns with clear calls to action and audience targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: plan and implement public service activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning and implementing public service activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate volunteerism and outreach that align with mission and strengthen public goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: establish and enforce codes of ethics and performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing and enforcing codes of ethics and standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create enforcement mechanisms and communicate adherence to bolster public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: disseminate governmental and other standards to members
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminating governmental and other standards to members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate regulatory and standards information into practical guidance for members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: conduct cooperative research
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting cooperative research: scientific, social, and economic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner on research projects that produce credible evidence for advocacy and member benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: place industry-level advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing advertisements on behalf of an entire industry, profession, or business endeavor; or on behalf of public health, safety, or welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan pooled-ad campaigns to promote sector-wide messages; coordinate funding and messaging across members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: promote positive employee relations and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting positive employee relations, accident prevention, and cooperation within an industry, profession, or other special-interest membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement internal communication and safety campaigns that reduce risk and foster cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activity: maintain internet and intranet sites for members and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining Internet and intranet sites serving current information needs of members and external stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure websites and intranets are current, user-friendly, and aligned with communications goals; use them as hubs for resources and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend: emphasize public affairs/advocacy and communications technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Association trends include growing emphasis on public affairs and advocacy communication directed to external constituents and on the use of communication technology to meet the information needs of members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in advocacy capabilities and digital platforms to keep pace with evolving expectations and to reach policymakers and publics effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor PR: identify target audiences and refine messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations in labor involves identifying new target audiences, establishing and maintaining key relationships, refining messages, building trust, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map audiences (members, public, policymakers, employers), tailor messaging to each, and sustain relationships to support campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor PR: use integrated research, social media, and traditional tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs management teams are now using research and social media along with traditional tools such as news releases, upgraded newsletters, and public service announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine data-driven research, social media engagement, and conventional media tactics to mobilize members, tell the union’s story, and gain public support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor PR: leverage labor’s power strategically even if unpopular
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic public relations in the labor movement often calls for leveraging labor’s position of power in ways that will not be universally popular but that will achieve labor’s goals for members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to pursue tactics that may provoke controversy if they are likely to advance core member interests; plan message framing and coalition-building accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider public opinion impacts when planning strikes
rubrics_metrics.description: Strikes may damage both sides: workers lose earnings, companies lose production and customers; media coverage tends to feature picket lines and vocal leaders; management is legally restricted in what it can say and do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh reputational and practical costs of strike action; use PR to manage narratives, prepare spokespeople, and mitigate long-term fallout.
